**Subject: AI utilisation in SAP ABAP delivery - PAL, ONGC (OVL) and T&G (cut-off 19 Nov 2026)**
Dear [Manager name],
As requested in your mail of 19 November, please find my report on AI utilisation in SAP ABAP delivery from 20 July to 19 November 2026. The AI tool used is Claude Code (Anthropic).

items: AI-assisted developments: 74 completed - ONGC (OVL) 51, T&G 12, PAL 6, common tools 5; 23 of them new developments.
Volume: 867 commits in under four months on 58 active days (including 6 weekends), 150,384 lines of code, 312 custom SAP objects, 17 technical specifications.

Significant applications: ONGC JIB Status management dashboard, DPR Fiori dashboard and CPI interface, bank revaluation and per-barrel analytics on CDS; PAL FB70 credit-memo approval workflow; T&G ZFORECAST (Adhesive and Paints), Exceptional Approval (WRICEF 141) and Clause 34 TDS report.
ATC (ONGC): 847 assigned findings remediated through 205 correction blocks in 51 includes across 14 packages, with 76 reusable correction patterns.
Automation: 17 automations and utilities - daily BP-creation mail, mass uploads, approval workflow, source mass-download and enhancement-finder tools.
Effort: 1,618 h conventional against 592 h with AI - **128 man-days saved, 63% effort reduction** (2.7x throughput).
Delivery: first working versions typically the same or next working day; JIB Status went from requirement (03/11) to written client confirmation (17/11) in 11 working days.
Benefit: three engagements handled concurrently, faster root-cause analysis on production issues, and reusable patterns and tools for the team.

1. Executive Summary

Between 20 July and 19 November 2026 AI (Claude Code) was integrated into my day-to-day SAP ABAP delivery on three concurrent projects - ONGC Videsh (OVL), T&G and PAL. **74 AI-assisted developments were completed**: 51 for ONGC, 12 for T&G, 6 for PAL and 5 common tools. They include complete applications (CDS / RAP dashboards, a credit-memo approval workflow, forecasting), new reports and interfaces, enhancements, ATC remediation of 51 program includes, root-cause analysis of production issues, and automation utilities.
The work produced **867 commits in under four months** - about 15 per active day - with 150,384 lines of code, 312 custom SAP objects and 17 technical specifications.

Conventional delivery of the same scope requires **1,618 hours**; with AI it took **592 hours** of my development time. **1,025 hours - 128 man-days - were saved, a 63% effort reduction and 2.7x delivery throughput.**
Strongest success story

ONGC Videsh Management Dashboard 'JIB Status': eight CDS views with an analytical cube, from requirement (03/11/26) to written client confirmation (17/11/26) in 11 working days; 60 h conventional effort delivered in 16 h (73% reduction).

blocks.text: Annex B - Effort Calculation and Assumptions
A. Effort without AI

Conventional effort per use case = baseline hours for the work type and complexity x scope factor (stated per use case where one delivery contains several objects). The baseline covers requirement understanding, technical analysis, design, coding, debugging, unit testing, rework and technical documentation. ATC uses the correction blocks actually applied: 10 / 25 / 40 minutes per pragma / replace / new-code block, 15 minutes per include, 8 h packaging.

blocks.caption: Conventional effort baseline by work type and complexity (hours)

blocks.text: B. Actual effort with AI

Actual effort counts the full development time of the period: 85 working days x 8 h, less the 13.5% share of status calls and transport administration (436 h from 19/08/26, plus dated work before it). It is distributed over the use cases by the measured AI session time of each object (commit timestamps), with a minimum per use case for prompting, review, activation and unit testing (2 / 4 / 8 / 16 h by complexity; 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 h for analyses). Review and correction time is therefore included in every figure.
C. Calculation methodology

items: Effort saved (hours) = effort without AI - actual effort with AI.
Effort reduction (%) = (effort saved / effort without AI) x 100.
Effort saved (man-days) = effort saved in hours / 8.
Productivity improvement (%) = ((effort without AI / actual effort with AI) - 1) x 100.
Project totals are weighted by hours (summed), not averaged percentages; recurring automation savings are kept separate from development savings.
